journey.blurb: Where the journey starts. Suya smoke, berbere, harissa and peanut stews.
Loomi, baharat and rose water. Feasts built for a long table.
Griddles, smokers and fryers, from Lima to New England.
Twenty regions pretending to be one cuisine. Dough, rice, cured pork.
Mostly technique. Good butter matters more than anything you buy.
A small pantry investment, then a lifetime of cheap dinners.
Pounded pastes, fish sauce, palm sugar, lime. Balance over heat.
The final port. Fry the spice paste until the oil separates.

recipes.title: Ethiopian Beef Tibs
recipes.description: Cubed beef seared hard with onion, chilli, and spiced butter, served on injera. Fast, loud, and usually cooked over very high heat in a clay dish that arrives still spitting.

items: 700 g beef sirloin or tenderloin, in 2.5 cm cubes
1 large red onion, cut in thick wedges
Injera, and awaze sauce to serve

ingredientGroups.group: Niter kibbeh, if making your own
items: 500 g butter simmered 30 min with garlic, ginger, cardamom, fenugreek, korerima, cinnamon, and nigella, then strained

method: Dry the beef thoroughly and season with salt. Wet meat steams instead of searing.
Get a heavy pan or cast iron dish very hot. Add the oil, then the beef in a single layer with space between the pieces.
Sear 90 seconds without touching it, then turn and sear another 60 seconds. Work in two batches. Remove.
Add the niter kibbeh, then the onion wedges, and cook 3 minutes so they char at the edges but keep their crunch.
Add the garlic, ginger, and chillies for 1 minute, then the berbere, mitmita, and cardamom for 30 seconds.
Splash in the wine, scraping the base, then return the beef with the tomato and rosemary.
Toss 60 seconds, taste for salt, and serve straight from the pan onto injera with awaze on the side.
recipes.cooksNote: Berbere burns quickly because of the sugar in the paprika. Add it near the end and keep everything moving.

recipes.title: Yassa Fish
recipes.description: The Senegalese onion, lemon, and mustard base, built around whole grilled fish rather than chicken. The fish gets marinated, grilled, then finished in the onions so it doesn't fall apart.

items: 4 whole fish, sea bream, tilapia, or mullet, 400 g each, scored
2 tbsp green olives and 1 tbsp capers, optional

method: Combine half the lemon juice, half the mustard, the garlic, salt, and pepper. Rub it into the fish, inside and into the score marks. Refrigerate 3 hours.
Toss the sliced onions with the remaining lemon juice, mustard, vinegar, and a good amount of salt. Let them sit while the fish marinates. They soften and lose their harshness.
Wipe the marinade off the fish and grill or pan-fry 4 minutes a side until browned. Set aside carefully.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and add the onions with all their liquid. Cook over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until soft, jammy, and pale gold.
Add the bay leaves, whole scotch bonnet, and stock. Simmer 10 minutes.
Lower the fish in, spoon onions over the top, cover, and simmer 8 minutes.
Add olives and capers, check the salt, and remove the scotch bonnet before serving over rice.
recipes.cooksNote: Leave the scotch bonnet whole and unpierced. It perfumes the sauce without making it inedibly hot, and you can always burst it at the end if you want more.

recipes.title: Chicken Suya
recipes.description: Nigerian grilled skewers coated in yaji, a spice mix built on ground peanuts. Sold from roadside grills at night, wrapped in newspaper with raw onion and tomato.

items: 800 g chicken breast or thigh, sliced into long thin strips
150 g roasted peanuts, or 120 g kuli kuli, ground to powder
2 tbsp cayenne or ground dried chilli
Sliced raw red onion, tomato, cucumber, extra yaji, lime

method: Grind the peanuts in short pulses until powdery. Stop before they turn into peanut butter, because oily yaji clumps and won't coat.
Blot the ground peanuts between paper towels to draw out some oil, then mix with the rest of the spices.
Toss the chicken with the oil and half the yaji. Marinate 2 hours in the fridge.
Thread the strips lengthwise onto skewers, keeping them flat.
Grill over hot coals or under a very hot broiler for 3 to 4 minutes a side. They cook fast, since the strips are thin.
Sprinkle the remaining dry yaji over the hot skewers as they come off. This second coating is where most of the flavour lives.
Serve with raw onion and tomato, extra yaji on the side, and lime.
recipes.cooksNote: Kuli kuli, the fried peanut snack, is the traditional base and it's already defatted. If you can find it, use it and skip the blotting.

recipes.title: Nkwobi
recipes.description: Cow foot in a thick palm oil sauce, emulsified with potash and flavoured with ehu seed. An Igbo delicacy, eaten with a cold beer and your hands.

items: 1.2 kg cow foot, cut into pieces by the butcher
2 onions, one chopped, one sliced for garnish
1 tsp powdered potash (akanwu), dissolved in 100 ml water and settled
1 tbsp ground ehu (calabash nutmeg) seeds, about 8 seeds toasted and ground
2 tbsp ground dried pepper or 3 scotch bonnets, blended

method: Wash the cow foot thoroughly, scraping the skin.
Boil with the chopped onion, stock cubes, and salt for 2 to 2½ hours until the skin is soft and gelatinous and the meat pulls from the bone. Top up water as needed.
Drain, reserving 150 ml of the cooking liquid.
Pour the palm oil into a clean pot. Carefully add the clear settled potash water, a spoonful at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
The oil will thicken and turn from red to a pale yellow-orange emulsion. Keep stirring until it looks like a thick sauce. Stop adding potash once it's there, because too much makes it soapy.
Stir in the ground ehu, pepper, crayfish, and a splash of the reserved stock over low heat.
Fold the cow foot through until every piece is coated. Serve in a wooden mortar, topped with utazi and onion rings.
recipes.cooksNote: Potash is strong stuff. Use the clear liquid only, never the sediment, and add it gradually. Bicarbonate of soda will emulsify the oil too, though it changes the flavour.

recipes.title: Chicken Brochettes
recipes.description: Grilled marinated skewers, a Central and East African staple sold everywhere from Kinshasa to Bujumbura. Usually served with fried plantain and a chilli sauce called pili pili.

items: 800 g chicken thigh, in 3 cm cubes
6 scotch bonnets, 4 garlic cloves, 1 small onion, 2 tbsp oil, juice of 1 lemon, salt, blended and briefly fried

method: Whisk the marinade and pour it over the chicken. Refrigerate at least 4 hours, overnight if you can.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, alternating with onion and pepper squares. Leave a little space between pieces so heat gets in.
Blend the pili pili ingredients, then fry the mixture in a small pan for 5 minutes to take the raw edge off. Cool.
Build a hot charcoal fire and let the flames settle to glowing coals.
Grill 10 to 12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, basting with leftover marinade only in the first half of cooking.
Move to a cooler part of the grill if the outsides char before the centre is done.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with fried plantain, rice, and plenty of pili pili.
recipes.cooksNote: Stop basting in the last five minutes. Raw marinade needs heat and time to become safe, and brushing it on at the end doesn't give it either.

recipes.title: Kuku Paka
recipes.description: Swahili coast chicken in coconut curry, grilled first for char then simmered in a coconut and lime sauce. The blend of East African and Indian cooking that defines the Kenyan and Tanzanian coast.

items: 1 chicken, jointed into 8, or 8 thighs, skin on
4 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, blended to a paste

method: Slash the chicken pieces, rub with the marinade, and rest 30 minutes.
Grill or broil the chicken until charred in patches and about three quarters cooked, roughly 15 minutes. The char is essential to the dish.
Meanwhile fry the onions in oil for 10 minutes until golden. Add garlic, ginger, and chillies for 2 minutes.
Add the dry spices, cook 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Blend half this base with a little coconut milk for a smoother sauce, then return it to the pan with the rest of the coconut milk.
Add the chicken and any juices from the grill tray. Simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and eggs to warm through, then finish with lime juice and a lot of chopped coriander. Serve with rice or chapati.
recipes.cooksNote: Don't skip the grilling step by simply frying the chicken. The smoky bitterness against the sweet coconut is the entire character of the dish.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce. North African in origin, adopted across the Middle East. Simple enough that the sauce needs to be genuinely good, not just quick.

items: 800 g tinned plum tomatoes, crushed by hand

method: Cook the onion and peppers in the oil over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until genuinely soft and sweet. Rushing this leaves the sauce sharp.
Add the garlic and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until it darkens.
Add the spices and harissa, cook 1 minute, then the tomatoes and sugar.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes until thick enough that a spoon dragged through leaves a trail that holds for a second. Season well.
Make wells with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Season the eggs themselves.
Cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Scatter feta and herbs and bring the pan to the table with bread.
recipes.cooksNote: Take it off the heat when the whites look almost but not quite set. Carryover cooking finishes them, and overcooked yolks defeat the purpose.

recipes.title: Harissa Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Roasted thighs under a harissa, honey, and lemon glaze. Weeknight food, one tray, and the skin gets properly crisp if you give it space.

items: 8 chicken thighs, bone in, skin on
Coriander, and yoghurt with lemon to serve

method: Whisk the harissa, oil, honey, lemon, garlic, spices, and salt.
Reserve 2 tbsp for the end, then coat the chicken with the rest and marinate at least an hour.
Toss the potatoes and onions with a little oil and salt and spread on a large tray.
Roast at 200°C for 20 minutes on their own.
Nestle the chicken on top, skin side up, leaving space between pieces so they roast rather than steam. Tuck in the lemon slices.
Roast 25 minutes, adding the tomatoes for the last 10.
Brush with the reserved harissa mixture and grill 3 minutes to glaze. Rest 5 minutes, scatter coriander, and serve with the lemon yoghurt.
recipes.cooksNote: Honey burns. Save the glaze for the last three minutes under the grill rather than putting it all on at the start.

recipes.title: Sukuma Wiki
recipes.description: Braised collard greens with onion and tomato, eaten daily across Kenya with ugali. The name translates roughly as "stretch the week," which tells you what it's for.

items: 600 g collard greens or kale, stems removed, rolled and sliced thin

method: Stack the leaves, roll them into a tight cigar, and slice across into thin ribbons. Uniform cutting matters more here than you'd think, since it's what makes them cook evenly.
Heat the oil and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and coriander and cook 5 minutes until they collapse into a rough sauce.
Add the greens in handfuls, stirring so each batch wilts before you add the next.
Pour in the water, add the stock cube, cover, and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until tender but still green.
Uncover, cook off any excess liquid, and finish with lemon juice. Serve with ugali and grilled meat.
recipes.cooksNote: Kale cooks faster than collards. If you're using kale, cut the covered simmer to five minutes or you'll end up with something grey and sad.

recipes.title: Pan-Seared Tilapia
recipes.description: A simple fillet with a spice crust, quick pan sauce, and lemon. Fifteen minutes start to finish, and the technique transfers to any firm white fish.

items: 2 tbsp plain flour or fine cornmeal
1 tsp salt, ½ tsp black pepper

method: Pat the fillets completely dry on both sides. This matters more than anything else in the recipe.
Mix the flour with all the dry spices and dust the fish lightly, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil in a non-stick or well-seasoned pan over medium-high until it shimmers.
Lay the fillets in presentation side down and press gently for 5 seconds so they make full contact.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes without moving them. When the edges turn opaque and the crust releases easily, flip once.
Cook 2 minutes more, then add the butter and garlic and baste the fish for 30 seconds as the butter foams.
Squeeze in the lemon off the heat, scatter parsley, and spoon the pan sauce over. Serve with rice or greens.
recipes.cooksNote: Tilapia is thin and goes from done to dry in under a minute. Pull it when the thickest part just flakes and no sooner.

recipes.title: Poulet Yassa
recipes.description: The chicken version of Senegal's yassa. Same onion, lemon, and mustard base as the fish, but the chicken marinates in it first and the onions cook down much longer.

items: 1 chicken, jointed into 8, or 8 thighs and drumsticks

method: Combine the onions, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add the chicken and turn everything so the onions are packed around it.
Refrigerate overnight, or at least 6 hours. The onions release water and soften in the acid.
Lift the chicken out, brushing the onions back into the bowl, and pat it dry.
Sear the chicken in oil until browned on all sides. Remove.
Add all the onions and marinade to the pot and cook over medium heat for 30 minutes, stirring often, until they collapse into a soft golden mass.
Add the stock, stock cubes, bay leaves, and whole scotch bonnet. Return the chicken, cover, and simmer 25 minutes.
Add olives and carrot for the last 5 minutes. Remove the scotch bonnet, check the seasoning, and serve over broken rice with the onions heaped on top.
recipes.cooksNote: Eight onions is correct and it isn't a typo. They reduce to about a quarter of their volume and they are the sauce, not a background ingredient.

recipes.title: Peppered Gizzard
recipes.description: Nigerian party food: chicken gizzards boiled tender, fried, then tossed in a fried pepper sauce. Chewy in a good way, and cheap.

items: 700 g chicken gizzards, cleaned and trimmed of silver skin
2 bay leaves, 1 stock cube, 1 tsp thyme, 1 tsp salt
2 onions, one blended and one sliced
4 tbsp neutral oil or palm oil
Spring onion and parsley to finish

method: Boil the gizzards with the onion, bay, thyme, stock cube, and salt for 40 to 50 minutes until tender enough to bite through cleanly. They'll never be soft, and they aren't meant to be.
Drain and dry them well, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
Shallow fry in hot oil for 4 minutes until browned and slightly crisp at the edges. Drain.
Blend the bell peppers, scotch bonnets, one onion, garlic, and ginger into a coarse purée.
Fry the sliced onion in oil for 5 minutes, add the tomato paste for 2 minutes, then pour in the blended pepper.
Fry the sauce over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring, until the water cooks off and the oil rises to the surface. This is the step people skip and it's the one that matters.
Season with the stock cube, curry powder, and thyme, then fold in the gizzards and cook 5 minutes. Finish with spring onion and parsley.
recipes.cooksNote: Raw blended pepper tastes sour and thin. You're looking for the sauce to darken and for oil to separate out at the edges, which takes a solid twenty minutes.

recipes.title: Peri-Peri Chicken Wings
recipes.description: Mozambican and South African chilli sauce built on African bird's eye chillies, lemon, and garlic. The sauce goes on twice: once as a marinade, once at the end.

items: 1.2 kg chicken wings, split into flats and drums
15 African bird's eye chillies, or 8 red chillies plus 3 scotch bonnets

method: Blend all the sauce ingredients except the bay leaves until smooth.
Simmer the sauce with the bay leaves for 15 minutes to cook out the raw onion and garlic. Cool, then split it in two.
Toss the dried wings with the baking powder and salt, then coat in half the sauce. Refrigerate 4 hours.
Arrange on a rack over a tray, spaced apart, and roast at 200°C for 25 minutes.
Turn and roast 12 minutes more until the skin is crisp and blistered.
Brush generously with the reserved fresh sauce.
Grill for 3 minutes to set the glaze, then serve with lemon wedges and more sauce for dipping.
recipes.cooksNote: The baking powder raises the skin's pH and helps it brown and crisp. It's a small amount and you won't taste it, but skip it and the wings come out noticeably softer.

recipes.title: Mafe
recipes.description: Senegalese groundnut stew. Peanut butter, tomato, and lamb or beef, cooked slowly until the oil separates. Rich, and one bowl goes a long way.

items: 1 kg lamb shoulder or beef chuck, in large cubes
2 carrots, 2 potatoes, 1 sweet potato, ½ small cabbage, cut into large chunks

method: Brown the meat hard in oil, in batches. Set aside.
Cook the onions for 10 minutes until golden, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and fry 3 minutes until it turns brick red and loses its metallic edge.
Loosen the peanut butter with a cup of warm stock, whisking until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Return the meat, add the remaining stock, stock cubes, bay, whole scotch bonnet, and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 1 hour, stirring often since peanut butter catches easily.
Add the root vegetables and cook 25 minutes, then the cabbage and okra for the last 10.
The stew is ready when a layer of peanut oil floats on the surface and the sauce coats a spoon. Remove the scotch bonnet, salt to taste, and serve over rice.
recipes.cooksNote: Stir the bottom of the pot every ten minutes or so. Peanut butter sinks and scorches, and burnt mafe is unrecoverable.

recipes.title: Fumbwa
recipes.description: Congolese wild spinach stewed with peanut and smoked fish. Fumbwa itself is a forest vine leaf, sold dried, and spinach is the usual stand-in outside Central Africa.

items: 200 g dried fumbwa leaves, soaked overnight, or 800 g fresh spinach
1 smoked mackerel or 200 g smoked fish, flaked, bones removed
150 g unsalted peanuts, ground, or 4 tbsp peanut butter
3 tomatoes, chopped, plus 2 tbsp tomato paste
Rice, fufu, or plantain to serve

method: If using dried fumbwa, soak overnight, then boil for 30 minutes until tender and drain. Fresh spinach needs only a quick blanch and a hard squeeze.
Chop the leaves finely.
Heat the palm oil until it just begins to shimmer, not smoke, then cook the onions for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, and chopped tomatoes, and cook 8 minutes until thick.
Stir in the ground peanuts loosened with a little water, plus the stock cube and scotch bonnet. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add the leaves and the smoked fish. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring, so the flavours combine and the sauce thickens around the greens.
Taste for salt. Smoked fish and stock cubes are both salty, so season last. Serve with rice, fufu, or fried plantain.
recipes.cooksNote: Overheating palm oil destroys its flavour and turns it acrid. Warm it gently and stop as soon as it loosens and moves freely in the pan.

recipes.title: Shawarma
recipes.description: Stacked marinated meat cooked on a vertical spit. At home, the honest version is a tightly packed loaf roasted in the oven and sliced thin, which gets you surprisingly close.

items: 1.2 kg boneless chicken thigh, skin on, or lamb shoulder sliced thin
200 g extra chicken skin or lamb fat
Flatbread, toum (garlic sauce), tahini sauce, pickled turnips, tomato, parsley, sumac onions

method: Slice the chicken into flat pieces of even thickness. Mix the marinade and rub it through. Refrigerate overnight.
Line a loaf tin with foil. Layer the meat in flat, alternating direction, with pieces of fat or skin every few layers. Press each layer down hard.
Fold the foil over, weigh it down with something heavy, and refrigerate 2 hours so it compacts.
Roast at 200°C for 40 minutes covered, then uncover and roast 30 minutes more until the top is dark and crusted.
Rest 20 minutes, then chill for an hour if you can. Cold meat slices far thinner.
Slice as thinly as your knife allows, then crisp the slices in a hot dry pan for 90 seconds.
Fill warm flatbread with meat, sauces, pickles, and onions. Roll tight and press on a hot pan to seal.
recipes.cooksNote: The fat layers aren't optional. Lean shawarma turns dry and stringy, and the rendered fat is what crisps the edges.

recipes.title: Kunafa Nabulsiyeh
recipes.description: Shredded pastry over stretchy cheese, soaked in syrup. The Nablus version uses a mild white cheese that has been soaked to draw out the salt. It should pull into strings when you cut it.

items: 700 g Nabulsi or Akkawi cheese, soaked, plus 200 g low-moisture mozzarella
Orange food colouring, traditional but optional

method: Soak the cheese in cold water for 4 to 6 hours, changing the water four times. Taste a piece: it should be mildly salty, not briny. Grate or slice it and drain well.
Make the syrup first. Boil the sugar and water for 8 minutes, add lemon juice, then take off the heat and stir in the flower waters. Cool it completely, because cold syrup on hot kunafa is the rule.
Pull the kataifi apart with your fingers and chop it into 1 cm lengths.
Work the melted ghee through it with your hands until every strand is coated and it looks slightly damp.
Press half the pastry firmly into a buttered 30 cm round pan. Press hard, all the way to the edges.
Spread the cheese over, leaving a 1 cm border, then cover with the rest of the pastry and press again.
Bake at 200°C for 35 to 40 minutes until the edges are deep gold. Invert onto a tray immediately, pour the cold syrup over while it's still hot, and scatter pistachios. Serve within the hour.
recipes.cooksNote: Cold syrup, hot kunafa. Reverse it and the pastry goes soggy instead of absorbing and staying crisp.

recipes.title: Qatayef
recipes.description: Small stuffed pancakes, cooked on one side only so the top stays open and spongy. Ramadan food, filled with either walnuts or sweet cheese, then fried or baked and soaked.

items: Walnut: 200 g walnuts, chopped, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp orange blossom water
Cheese: 300 g ashta or ricotta mixed with soaked Akkawi
300 g sugar, 180 ml water, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp rose water

method: Blend all the batter ingredients until completely smooth. It should be thinner than pancake batter, closer to double cream. Rest 1 hour until bubbly.
Make the syrup and cool it.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium with no oil. Pour in 2 tbsp of batter and let it spread into a 9 cm circle.
Cook one side only. Bubbles will rise and burst across the surface. When the top looks completely dry and matte, about 90 seconds, lift it off. Never flip it.
Cool the pancakes on a cloth, uncovered, so they don't steam and go slippery.
Put a spoonful of filling on the cooked side, fold in half, and pinch the edge closed from one end to the other. It should seal with just pressure.
Fry at 175°C for 2 minutes until golden, or bake at 200°C with a brush of ghee for 15 minutes. Dip straight into cold syrup, then pistachios.
recipes.cooksNote: If the edges won't seal, the pancakes have dried out too long. Cover them with a slightly damp cloth for a few minutes and try again.

recipes.title: Mansaf
recipes.description: Jordan's national dish: lamb cooked in fermented dried yoghurt called jameed, served over rice and flatbread. Eaten communally from one platter, traditionally with the right hand.

items: 2 kg lamb shoulder or leg, on the bone, in large pieces
500 g jameed, broken and soaked overnight in 1.5 litres water
3 bay leaves, 6 cardamom pods, 2 cinnamon sticks, 1 tbsp black peppercorns
2 large sheets shrak or markook bread
150 g toasted almonds and pine nuts

method: Blend the soaked jameed with its water until smooth, then strain through a sieve. Set aside.
Brown the lamb in ghee in batches. Add the onions, whole spices, turmeric, and baharat, then cover with water and simmer 2 hours until tender. Skim regularly.
Lift the lamb out. Strain and reserve 500 ml of the cooking broth.
Heat the jameed liquid in a large pot, stirring constantly in one direction until it comes to a bare simmer. It must not boil or it will split.
Add the lamb and the reserved broth and simmer very gently for 30 minutes. Season.
Cook the rice with ghee, a pinch of turmeric, and salt.
Line a large platter with the bread, ladle some jameed sauce over to soften it, then rice, then lamb on top. Pour more sauce over, scatter nuts and parsley, and serve the remaining sauce in bowls.
recipes.cooksNote: Stirring in one direction while the jameed heats is a real technique, not folklore. It keeps the yoghurt proteins from separating.

recipes.title: Dajaj Mashwi
recipes.description: Grilled chicken with garlic, lemon, and spice, served with toum. It's what a Levantine rotisserie shop sells all day, and the marinade does most of the work.

items: 1 head garlic, peeled and green germs removed

method: Slash the chicken through the thickest parts of the thigh and breast. Rub the marinade in everywhere and refrigerate 6 hours or overnight.
For toum, blend the garlic and salt to a paste, scraping down twice.
With the machine running, add the oil in a slow thread, alternating with the lemon juice. Start with literal drops. Adding oil too fast is the only way this fails.
Finish with the ice water to set it. It should be white, thick, and stiff enough to hold a peak.
Set up a grill with two zones. Cook the chicken skin side up on the indirect side, covered, for 30 minutes.
Move it over the coals skin side down for 8 minutes, watching for flare-ups from the oil.
Rest 10 minutes. Serve with toum, flatbread, pickles, and a sumac onion salad.
recipes.cooksNote: If the toum splits, put a tablespoon of the broken mixture in a clean bowl with a spoonful of ice water and slowly beat the rest back into it.

recipes.title: Laddu
recipes.description: Chickpea flour balls with ghee, sugar, and cardamom. Indian in origin and completely at home in Muscat and Dubai, where it's sold beside halwa in the same sweet shops.

items: Generous pinch saffron, soaked in 1 tbsp warm milk

method: Fry the nuts and raisins in 2 tbsp ghee until golden. Remove and set aside.
Melt the remaining ghee in a heavy pan over low heat and add the besan.

Roast it, stirring constantly, for 20 to 25 minutes. It goes from pale yellow to sandy to golden brown, and the smell changes completely, from raw and dusty to nutty. That smell is the only reliable signal.
Take it off the heat and let it cool to just above body temperature. Too hot and the sugar melts into syrup.
Stir in the sugar, cardamom, saffron milk, nuts, and raisins.
Squeeze a handful in your palm to test. If it holds, start rolling. If it crumbles, add a tablespoon of warm ghee.
Roll into balls about 40 g each, pressing firmly. Cool completely on a tray. They firm up as they sit and keep two weeks in a tin.
recipes.cooksNote: Low heat and constant stirring for the full 25 minutes. Under-roasted besan tastes raw and chalky, and no amount of sugar hides it.

recipes.title: Sayadiyah
recipes.description: Fish with rice cooked in caramelised onion stock. The onions are cooked far past golden, almost to the edge of burnt, and that darkness is the entire flavour and colour of the dish.

items: 1 kg firm white fish, hamour, grouper, or sea bass, in thick steaks
2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp allspice
100 g toasted pine nuts and almonds
150 g tahini, juice of 2 lemons, 2 garlic cloves crushed, water to loosen, salt

method: Season the fish with salt, half the cumin, and lemon. Rest 20 minutes.
Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 30 to 35 minutes. Keep going past golden until they're a deep coffee brown, but stop before anything turns black and bitter.
Lift out a third of the onions and drain them for the garnish.
Add the remaining spices to the pot, cook 1 minute, then add the water. Simmer 10 minutes and blend, or push through a sieve, into a dark savoury stock.
Fry the fish in a separate pan until browned on both sides but not cooked through. Set aside.
Drain the rice and add it to the stock in a ratio of about 1 part rice to 1.5 parts liquid. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook 15 minutes on the lowest heat.
Lay the fish on top for the last 8 minutes so it steams through. Rest 10 minutes, then serve topped with the reserved onions, nuts, and tahini sauce.
recipes.cooksNote: Judging the onions is the skill. Pull one out and taste it: sweet and deeply savoury is right, sharply bitter means you went too far and the whole dish will taste of it.

recipes.title: Ma'amoul
recipes.description: Semolina shortbread stuffed with dates, walnuts, or pistachios, pressed in carved wooden moulds. Made in large batches before Eid and Easter.

items: Date: 400 g date paste worked with 2 tbsp ghee and 1 tsp cinnamon
Walnut: 300 g walnuts, 80 g sugar, 1 tbsp orange blossom water, 1 tsp cinnamon
Pistachio: 300 g pistachios, 80 g sugar, 1 tbsp rose water

method: Rub the melted ghee into the semolinas and flour with your hands until every grain is coated. Cover and leave overnight at room temperature. This rest is what makes the texture sandy rather than hard.
Next day, dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and add it with the flower waters and mahlab. Knead lightly, just until it holds. Overworking makes them tough.
Rest 30 minutes. Roll each filling into small balls, about 10 g each.
Take 25 g of dough, roll it into a ball, and press your thumb into the centre to make a cup.
Put a filling ball in and pinch the dough closed over it, then roll smooth.
Press into a floured ma'amoul mould, then knock it out firmly onto a lined tray. If you don't have moulds, flatten slightly and decorate with a fork or tweezers.
Bake at 170°C for 15 to 18 minutes. They should stay pale, with only the base coloured. Cool completely, then dust the nut ones with icing sugar.
recipes.cooksNote: Browned ma'amoul are overbaked. Pull them out while they still look underdone, because they firm up considerably as they cool.

recipes.title: Ogaily (Ageeli)
recipes.description: A Bahraini saffron and cardamom cake, topped with sesame and nigella seeds. Dense, fragrant, and served with tea. It's sometimes just called Bahraini cake.

items: 1 tsp saffron threads, ground and soaked in 3 tbsp warm rose water

method: Grind the saffron with a pinch of sugar in a mortar, then soak in the warm rose water for 15 minutes. Grinding first extracts far more colour.
Beat the eggs and sugar for 5 minutes until pale and thickened.
Pour in the oil in a steady stream while beating, then the milk and the saffron water.
Sift in the flour, semolina, baking powder, cardamom, turmeric, and salt. Fold until just combined and no streaks remain.
Pour into a lined 24 cm tin. Let it stand 10 minutes so the semolina hydrates.
Scatter the sesame, nigella, and pistachios generously over the surface.
Bake at 175°C for 40 to 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin 15 minutes, then turn out. Better on day two.
recipes.cooksNote: Real saffron is expensive and this cake uses a lot of it. The turmeric is there to carry the colour so you can use a lighter hand with the saffron without ending up with a pale cake.

recipes.title: Shuraik
recipes.description: A sweet enriched bread ring, crusted with sesame and nigella seeds. Eaten across the Hejaz and Sudan, especially at Eid, and it keeps well for a few days.

items: ½ tsp ground fennel or anise, optional

method: Whisk the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, cardamom, and fennel together.
Add the eggs, ghee, rose water, and warm milk. Mix into a soft dough.
Knead 10 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky. It should pull away from the bowl but still stick lightly to your fingers.
Cover and rise 90 minutes until doubled.
Divide into 8. Roll each into a rope about 30 cm long, then join the ends into a ring, pressing the join firmly.
Set on lined trays, cover, and prove 40 minutes until puffy.
Brush with egg wash, press sesame and nigella seeds over the top, and bake at 180°C for 18 to 20 minutes until deep golden. Cool on a rack.
recipes.cooksNote: Press the seeds down with your palm after scattering them. If you just sprinkle, most end up on the tray.

recipes.title: Muhammar
recipes.description: Bahraini sweet rice with dates and date syrup, served with fried or grilled fish. The sweet and savoury combination sounds odd and works completely.

items: 100 g soft dates, pitted and chopped
1 tsp saffron, soaked in 3 tbsp rose water
6 fish steaks, salted, dusted in turmeric and flour, and fried

method: Boil a large pot of salted water with the cardamom pods and cinnamon stick.
Drain the soaked rice and boil it for 5 to 6 minutes only, until the outside is soft and the centre is still hard. Drain immediately.
Warm the date syrup with the ghee, chopped dates, sugar, and ground cardamom until loose and pourable.
Spread a third of the date mixture in the base of a heavy pot with a little ghee.
Layer in the rice, drizzling the rest of the date mixture and the saffron rose water between layers. Don't stir it in, or the whole pot turns uniformly brown.
Poke a few holes down through the rice with a spoon handle, cover the pot with a cloth-wrapped lid, and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes.
Turn out so the caramelised bottom layer ends up on top. Scatter sesame seeds and serve with the fried fish alongside.
recipes.cooksNote: A cloth under the lid catches condensation. Without it the water drips back down and you lose the crust at the bottom.

recipes.title: Aseedah
recipes.description: A smooth cooked wheat dough, served in a mound with a well of butter and honey or date syrup in the middle. Eaten across Yemen, Oman, and Sudan, and it's a workout to make.

items: 300 g plain wheat flour, or a mix of wheat and barley

method: Bring 600 ml of the water to a boil with the salt.
Whisk the flour into the remaining 150 ml of cold water into a smooth slurry with no lumps.
Pour the slurry into the boiling water while whisking hard. It'll thicken fast.
Reduce the heat to low. Now switch to a sturdy wooden spoon and beat the dough continuously for 15 to 20 minutes, pressing it against the sides of the pot and folding it over.
It's done when it pulls away from the sides cleanly and comes together as one smooth glossy mass with no raw flour taste.
Wet a bowl, press the dough in, then turn it out onto a plate to make a dome. Make a deep well in the top with the back of a wet spoon.
Fill the well with melted ghee and honey, dust with cardamom, and eat from the outside in with your fingers, dipping each piece.
recipes.cooksNote: Your arm will hurt. That's the recipe working. Stopping early leaves you with lumpy paste that tastes of raw flour.

recipes.title: Saloona
recipes.description: The everyday Gulf stew: meat or fish with vegetables, tomato, loomi, and baharat, served over rice. Every household has a slightly different version and none of them are wrong.

items: 800 g lamb shoulder or chicken thigh, in chunks
4 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, made into a paste
3 tomatoes, chopped, plus 2 tbsp tomato paste
2 potatoes, 2 carrots, 1 courgette, 1 aubergine, all in chunks
2 loomi, pierced, or 1 tsp loomi powder
1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp cinnamon

method: Brown the meat in ghee in a heavy pot, in batches so it colours rather than steams.
Add the onions and cook 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger paste, then the spices, and fry 90 seconds until the smell turns from raw to toasty.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then the fresh tomatoes until they break down.
Return the meat with the stock, loomi, and chillies. Simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add the root vegetables and cook 15 minutes, then the courgette and aubergine for a final 12 minutes so they don't disintegrate.
Fish out the loomi if you like, since they get bitter if left too long. Season, scatter coriander, and serve over rice.
recipes.cooksNote: Adding the vegetables in stages instead of all at once is the difference between a stew and a mush. Hardest first, softest last.

recipes.title: Mufattah
recipes.description: Spiced rice with fish, built over a base of thin flatbread that soaks up everything that runs down. A Gulf coastal dish, plain in principle and generous in practice.

items: 1.2 kg firm white fish, hamour or snapper, in steaks
2 large sheets thin flatbread (raqaq or markook)
1 tbsp baharat, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander
1 tsp saffron in 3 tbsp rose water
60 g raisins and 60 g toasted almonds

method: Season the fish with salt, turmeric, and lemon. Rest 20 minutes, then fry in ghee until browned on both sides. Set aside without cooking it through.
In the same pot, fry the onions for 15 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic and dry spices, cook 1 minute, then the tomatoes and loomi. Cook until pulpy.
Add the stock and simmer 10 minutes to build a flavoured broth. Taste and salt it well.
Drain the rice, add it to the broth, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Drizzle the saffron rose water over the surface, lay the fish on top, cover, and steam 10 minutes more.
Line a large platter with the flatbread, spoon the rice over it, arrange the fish on top, and finish with raisins, almonds, and coriander. Serve lemon on the side.
recipes.cooksNote: Tear the bread rather than cutting it, and let it sit under the rice for a few minutes before serving so it softens without turning to paste.

recipes.title: Fatoot
recipes.description: Yemeni torn flatbread fried with eggs, tomato, and chilli. Breakfast, or dinner when you have leftover bread and nothing else. It takes ten minutes.

items: 3 stale flatbreads, or 1 large khubz, torn into rough pieces
1 tsp hawaij spice mix, if you have it

method: Tear the bread into pieces roughly the size of a large coin. Stale is better than fresh, because it holds shape instead of dissolving.
Melt the ghee and fry the bread pieces for 4 minutes until they crisp at the edges. Lift them out.
Add the onion to the pan and cook 4 minutes, then the garlic and chillies for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook until they collapse into a rough sauce.
Return the bread and toss so it soaks up some of the sauce but keeps a bit of texture.
Beat the eggs, season them, and pour over. Fold gently with a spatula until just set, still glossy.
Take it off the heat while it looks slightly underdone, since it keeps cooking in the pan. Coriander over the top, zhoug on the side.
recipes.cooksNote: Frying the bread separately first is worth the extra step. Add it raw and the whole thing turns into a soggy scramble.

recipes.title: Birria Tacos
recipes.description: Slow-braised chilli beef, shredded into tortillas dipped in the fat from the braise, griddled until crisp, and served with a cup of consommé for dunking.

items: 1.5 kg beef chuck, plus 1 kg beef short rib or shin on the bone
6 guajillo chillies, 4 ancho chillies, 2 chiles de árbol, all stemmed and seeded
4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 peppercorns, 2 bay leaves
400 g Oaxaca cheese or low-moisture mozzarella, shredded

method: Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side. They should smell fragrant and soften slightly. Any smoke means burnt, and burnt chillies taste bitter through the whole pot.
Cover the chillies with boiling water and soak 20 minutes.
Char the onion, garlic, and tomatoes in the same dry pan until blackened in patches.
Blend the drained chillies with the charred vegetables, vinegar, spices, salt, and a cup of the soaking water until completely smooth. Push it through a sieve.
Sear the beef hard, then combine with the chilli purée and stock in a heavy pot. It should be nearly covered.
Cover and cook at 160°C for 3½ to 4 hours until the meat shreds under a fork.

Skim the red fat off the top and reserve it. Shred the meat. Dip a tortilla in that fat, lay it on a hot griddle, add cheese and meat, fold, and fry 2 minutes a side until crisp. Serve with consommé, onion, coriander, and lime.
recipes.cooksNote: Sieving the chilli purée takes five minutes and removes all the skin fragments. It's the single biggest upgrade to the texture of the consommé.

recipes.title: Tres Leches Cake
recipes.description: A sponge built to absorb, soaked in three milks and topped with whipped cream. The cake must be dry and open-crumbed, which is why there's no butter in it.
method: Beat the yolks with three quarters of the sugar until pale and thick, about 5 minutes. Add the milk and vanilla.
Fold in the sifted flour, baking powder, and salt.
Whip the whites to soft peaks, add the remaining sugar, and beat to firm peaks. Fold into the batter in three additions.
Pour into a lined 23 by 33 cm tin and bake at 175°C for 25 to 30 minutes until springy and golden.
Cool completely in the tin. Poke holes all over with a skewer, going right to the base.
Whisk the three milks together and pour slowly over the cake, a third at a time, waiting for each to soak in. It will look like too much liquid. It isn't.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight. Whip the topping cream with icing sugar, spread thickly, and dust with cinnamon.
recipes.cooksNote: Soak a cooled cake, never a warm one. Warm sponge turns gummy and won't take the liquid evenly.

recipes.title: Lomo Saltado
recipes.description: Peru's Chinese-Peruvian stir fry: beef, onion, tomato, and chips, tossed in soy and vinegar, served with rice. Yes, chips and rice on the same plate. That's the dish.

items: 600 g beef sirloin or tenderloin, in thick strips
2 red onions, cut into thick wedges
1 ají amarillo, sliced, plus 1 tbsp ají amarillo paste
600 g potatoes, cut into thick chips and fried

method: Fry the chips until golden and crisp. Drain and keep warm. They must be ready before you start the stir fry.
Season the beef heavily with salt and pepper. Dry it well.
Get a wok or wide pan as hot as it will go. Add oil, then the beef in a single layer. Leave it 60 seconds to sear before moving it.
Cook 2 minutes total, then remove. It should be rare in the middle.
Add the onions and ají amarillo and cook 90 seconds. They should stay crunchy at the core.
Add the garlic for 15 seconds, then the vinegar and soy, letting it hiss and reduce. Add the ají paste and oyster sauce.
Return the beef with the tomatoes, toss 30 seconds, then fold in the chips and coriander at the very end. Serve immediately with rice.
recipes.cooksNote: Everything happens fast, so have all your ingredients cut and lined up before you turn on the heat. The onions and tomatoes should still have bite.

recipes.title: Chicha Morada
recipes.description: Purple corn drink, boiled with pineapple skin, cinnamon, and clove, then sweetened and sharpened with lime. Non-alcoholic and served with almost everything in Peru.

items: 500 g dried purple corn (maíz morado), whole cobs or kernels
Skin and core of 1 pineapple, well washed
Finely diced apple and pineapple, to serve

method: Rinse the corn. If using whole cobs, break them into pieces so the cob goes in too, since it carries a lot of the colour.
Put the corn, water, pineapple skin, apple, and whole spices in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 45 minutes. The water turns dark purple, almost black.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth, pressing the solids gently. Discard everything solid.
Cool to room temperature, then stir in the sugar until dissolved. Taste as you go, since sweetness is personal here.
Add the lime juice last. It brightens the flavour and shifts the colour slightly toward red.
Chill thoroughly and serve over ice with the diced fruit floating in it.
recipes.cooksNote: Add lime only after the liquid has cooled. Hot lime juice tastes cooked and slightly bitter.

recipes.title: Tallarines Verdes
recipes.description: Peruvian green pasta, related to pesto but built on spinach and evaporated milk rather than pine nuts and oil. Creamier, milder, and usually served with a fried steak on top.

items: 250 g spinach, blanched 30 seconds and squeezed dry
100 g queso fresco, or feta rinsed of salt

method: Fry the onion and garlic in the olive oil until soft and lightly golden, about 8 minutes. Cool slightly.
Blend the spinach, basil, cooked onion and garlic, nuts, both cheeses, and the evaporated milk until smooth and bright green.
Season well. It should taste slightly too strong on its own, since the pasta will mute it.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve a cup of the water.
Warm the sauce gently in a wide pan. Do not boil it, or the milk will split and the green will dull.
Drain the pasta and toss it into the sauce with a splash of pasta water until it coats evenly.
Season the steaks, fry them hard for 90 seconds a side, and serve on top of the pasta.
recipes.cooksNote: Blanching the spinach and squeezing it very dry keeps the sauce from being watery and keeps the colour vivid. Raw spinach gives a greyer result.

recipes.title: Pescado Frito
recipes.description: Whole fried fish, coastal Latin America's default plate, served with rice, patacones, and a sharp salad. Crisp skin, moist flesh, lime everywhere.

items: 4 whole fish, mojarra, snapper, or sea bream, 400 g each, scaled and gutted
Patacones (twice-fried green plantain), coconut rice, lime wedges
Salad of tomato, red onion, coriander, lime, and salt

method: Score each fish three times per side, cutting down to the bone.
Rub with garlic, lime juice, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper, working it into the cuts. Rest 30 minutes.
Pat the fish dry on the outside. The marinade stays in the cuts, but the skin needs to be dry.
Mix the cornmeal and flour and dredge each fish, pressing it into the scores.
Heat 3 cm of oil to 180°C in a wide pan.
Fry 6 to 7 minutes on the first side without moving it, then turn once and fry 5 minutes more. The fin should pull out easily when it's done.
Drain on a rack, salt lightly, and serve with everything else and a lot of lime.
recipes.cooksNote: Fry one fish at a time unless your pan is enormous. Two fish drop the oil temperature and you get greasy skin instead of crisp.

recipes.title: Papa a la Huancaína
recipes.description: Boiled potatoes under a creamy ají amarillo sauce. A starter, and one of the easiest ways into Peruvian food since it takes fifteen minutes.

items: 1 kg yellow potatoes, boiled whole in salted water, peeled and sliced thick
4 ají amarillo, seeded and deveined, or 4 tbsp ají amarillo paste
Boiled eggs, black olives, lettuce leaves

method: If using fresh ají, boil the chillies three times in fresh water, 5 minutes each time, draining between. This removes most of the heat while keeping the fruity flavour.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes, then add the ají and cook 3 minutes more.
Blend that mixture with the cheese, evaporated milk, and crackers until completely smooth.
Check the consistency. It should pour slowly and coat a spoon thickly. Add milk to loosen or another cracker to thicken.
Season with salt. Chill for at least 30 minutes so it firms slightly.
Lay lettuce on plates, arrange the potato slices over it.
Pour the sauce over generously and top each plate with a halved boiled egg and a few olives.
recipes.cooksNote: Crackers are the real thickener. They're not a shortcut, they're the traditional method, and bread doesn't behave the same way.

recipes.title: Crispy Colombian Empanadas
recipes.description: Corn dough shells with potato and beef inside, deep fried until the outside shatters. The dough is masarepa, not wheat, which is why the texture is so different from Argentine empanadas.

items: 1 tbsp achiote or ½ tsp turmeric
400 g potatoes, boiled and roughly mashed
300 g minced beef, or beef and pork
1 onion, 3 spring onions, 2 tomatoes, all finely chopped
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp achiote, ½ tsp black pepper
Chopped spring onion, coriander, lime juice, vinegar, water, chopped chilli, salt

method: Cook the onion, spring onion, garlic, and tomato in oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and spices, brown it well, then fold in the mashed potato and coriander. Season firmly and cool completely.
Mix the masarepa with the water, achiote, salt, and oil. Knead 3 minutes, then rest 10 minutes. It should feel like soft playdough, smooth with no cracks when you roll a ball.
Cut a plastic bag open. Put a golf-ball-sized piece of dough between the sheets and press flat to 3 mm with a plate.
Spoon filling onto one half, then use the plastic to fold the dough over and seal, pressing the edge firmly. Trim with a bowl rim for a neat half-moon.
Heat oil to 180°C. Fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and blistered.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with ají.
recipes.cooksNote: If the dough cracks when folded, it's too dry. Work in a tablespoon of warm water at a time until it stops.

recipes.title: Chicken Burrito Bowls
recipes.description: Not traditional anything, but a genuinely good weeknight assembly. Everything can be made ahead and the components keep separately for four days.

items: 3 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp chipotle in adobo
2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp salt
Juice of 1 lime, large handful chopped coriander, 1 tbsp oil, salt
1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 bay leaf, 200 ml stock
Pico de gallo, corn salsa, guacamole, sour cream, grated cheese, shredded lettuce, pickled red onion

method: Blend the chicken marinade and coat the thighs. Leave 30 minutes minimum, longer if you have it.
Cook the rice with the bay leaf and salt. When done, fluff and fold through the lime juice, oil, and coriander while still hot.
Fry the onion and garlic for the beans, add cumin, beans, bay leaf, and stock, and simmer 15 minutes until thickened. Mash a spoonful against the side to give it body.
Sear the chicken in a very hot pan or on a grill, 5 minutes a side, until charred at the edges.
Rest 5 minutes, then chop into rough pieces.
Warm the bowls if you're being nice about it.
Build in order: rice, beans, chicken, then everything cold on top. Squeeze lime over at the end.
recipes.cooksNote: Salt each component separately as you go. A bowl seasoned only at the end tastes flat in the middle no matter how much you add on top.

recipes.title: Chilaquiles
recipes.description: Fried tortillas simmered briefly in salsa, topped with egg, cheese, and cream. Breakfast, and the classic use for stale tortillas. Timing is everything, since they go soggy fast.

items: 16 corn tortillas, cut into 6 wedges each, ideally a day old
6 tomatoes, 4 guajillo chillies, 2 chiles de árbol

method: Fry the tortilla wedges in batches at 180°C until golden and rigid. Drain on paper and salt lightly. Baking at 200°C with a little oil for 15 minutes also works.
Toast the dried chillies briefly, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes.
Char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic under a hot grill until blistered and blackened in spots.
Blend everything with the cumin, oregano, and a little soaking water until smooth.
Fry the salsa in 2 tbsp of hot oil for 5 minutes so it darkens and thickens, then add the stock and simmer 10 minutes. Season.
Bring the salsa to a hard simmer, add the chips, and fold for 60 to 90 seconds only. They should be coated and softening at the edges but still have structure.
Get them onto plates immediately with egg, cheese, crema, onion, coriander, and avocado.
recipes.cooksNote: Serve within two minutes of adding the chips. Chilaquiles have a short window between perfect and mush, and there's no way to slow it down.

recipes.title: Classic Cheeseburger
recipes.description: Two thin patties, American cheese, soft bun. The smashing technique gives you a crust across the whole surface, which is where the flavour lives.

items: 600 g ground beef chuck, 20% fat, loosely formed into 8 balls of 75 g
Sliced dill pickles, thin white onion, shredded lettuce, tomato
4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp yellow mustard, 2 tbsp chopped pickle, 1 tsp pickle brine, ½ tsp paprika

method: Handle the beef as little as possible. Roll each portion loosely into a ball and don't compact it.
Mix the sauce and chill it. Butter and toast the cut sides of the buns in a pan until golden.
Get a cast iron pan or flat griddle screaming hot. Wipe it with a little oil.
Place two balls on the surface, wait 10 seconds, then smash each flat with a stiff spatula, hard, to about 1 cm. Hold for 5 seconds.
Season the top with salt and pepper. Cook 90 seconds until the edges are dark brown and lacy.
Scrape underneath with a sharp-edged spatula so all the crust comes with it, flip, and add cheese immediately. Cook 45 seconds more.
Stack two patties per bun with sauce, pickles, onion, lettuce, and tomato. Eat right away.
recipes.cooksNote: Smash within the first 30 seconds or not at all. Once the surface has set, pressing just squeezes out juice and gives you a dry patty.

recipes.title: Crab Imperial
recipes.description: A Chesapeake Bay classic: lump crab meat bound in a light mayonnaise mixture and baked until golden. The whole point is minimal binder and maximum crab.

items: 500 g jumbo lump blue crab meat, picked over gently for shell

method: Whisk the mayonnaise, yolk, mustard, Worcestershire, Old Bay, and lemon juice into a smooth binder.
Fold in the red pepper and parsley.
Add the crab and fold with a rubber spatula, lifting from underneath, using no more than six or seven strokes. The lumps must stay whole, because broken crab turns the dish into a paste.
Divide between four ramekins or scallop shells, mounding it rather than pressing it flat.
Drizzle with the melted butter and scatter panko over if you want a crunchy top.
Dust with paprika and bake at 190°C for 15 to 18 minutes until the tops are golden and the centre is hot.
Rest 3 minutes and serve with lemon and nothing else that competes.
recipes.cooksNote: Pick through the crab with your fingers rather than a fork. You'll find the shell fragments and you won't shred the meat doing it.

recipes.title: New England Clam Chowder
recipes.description: Thick, white, and made with salt pork or bacon. The clam liquor is the base, so don't throw it away, and don't add flour so heavily that it turns to wallpaper paste.

items: 2 kg fresh quahogs or littleneck clams, scrubbed, or 500 g chopped clams plus 500 ml clam juice
250 ml water or dry white wine
120 g salt pork or thick bacon, diced
700 g floury potatoes, in 2 cm cubes

method: Steam the clams with the water in a covered pot for 6 to 8 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Strain the liquid through a cloth to catch grit, and keep every drop. Chop the clam meat.
Render the salt pork in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp. Lift out the crisp bits and reserve.
Cook the onion and celery in the fat for 8 minutes without browning. Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Add the clam liquor gradually, whisking, then the potatoes, bay, and thyme. Simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and some have started to break down and thicken things.
Add the milk and cream and bring to a bare simmer. Never let it boil.
Add the chopped clams and butter, heat through for 2 minutes only, and season with white pepper. Serve with the crisp pork, chives, and crackers.
recipes.cooksNote: Clams toughen in about a minute of hard cooking. They go in last, and the pot comes off the heat right after.

recipes.title: Maine Lobster Roll
recipes.description: Cold lobster in a light dressing, in a griddled split-top bun. The Connecticut version uses warm butter instead. Both are good, but this is the Maine one.

items: 4 live lobsters, 500 g each, or 500 g cooked lobster meat

method: Boil the lobsters in heavily salted water for 8 minutes, then plunge into ice water to stop the cooking.
Pick out the tail, claw, and knuckle meat. Knuckle meat is the sweetest and most people throw it out.
Cut into large chunks, roughly 2 cm. Chopping it small ruins the whole experience.
Chill the meat thoroughly, at least an hour.
Toss gently with the mayonnaise, lemon, celery, chives, celery salt, and pepper. Use just enough mayo to coat, not to bind. You should still see lobster, not dressing.
Butter the flat outer sides of the buns and griddle in a pan until golden and crisp on both sides.
Line with lettuce if you like, then fill generously so the meat sits above the rim. Eat immediately.
recipes.cooksNote: Dress it right before serving. Lobster sitting in mayonnaise for an hour goes watery and loses its texture.

recipes.title: Poutine
recipes.description: Chips, cheese curds, gravy. Quebec's contribution to the world, and the details that matter are fresh squeaky curds and a gravy hot enough to soften them without melting them into soup.

items: 1.2 kg floury potatoes, cut into 1 cm chips
400 g fresh cheese curds, at room temperature

method: Soak the cut chips in cold water for 30 minutes, then dry them completely.
Make a roux: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until it turns the colour of peanut butter.
Add both stocks gradually, whisking out lumps as you go. Add ketchup, vinegar, Worcestershire, and pepper.
Simmer 15 minutes until it coats a spoon. Season and keep it hot.
Fry the chips at 150°C for 5 minutes until soft and pale. Drain and cool at least 20 minutes.
Raise the oil to 190°C and fry again for 3 minutes until deep golden and crunchy. Salt immediately.
Pile the chips in a bowl, scatter the curds over, and pour the very hot gravy on top. Serve at once.
recipes.cooksNote: Cold curds won't soften properly. Take them out of the fridge an hour ahead, and don't substitute grated mozzarella, since the squeak is half the reason poutine exists.

recipes.title: Texas Smoked Brisket
recipes.description: Salt, pepper, oak smoke, twelve hours. Central Texas barbecue is deliberately minimal, which means there's nothing to hide behind.

items: 1 whole packer brisket, 5 to 6 kg, point and flat attached

method: Trim the fat cap to about 6 mm, remove the hard deckle fat between the muscles, and round off the edges so nothing thin sticks out to burn.
Mix the rub and coat every surface heavily. It should look like the meat is wearing a coat. Rest at room temperature 1 hour.
Get the smoker steady at 120°C with clean thin blue smoke. Thick white smoke means bad combustion and it will make the meat taste acrid.
Put the brisket on fat side up, point end toward the fire. Leave it alone for 6 hours.
Around 70°C internal, the temperature will stop climbing. This is the stall, it's evaporative cooling, and it can last 4 hours. Wait it out or wrap through it.
Wrap tightly in butcher paper once the bark is dark and firm and doesn't smudge when you touch it. Return to the smoker.

Pull at 96 to 99°C, when a probe slides into the flat like it's going into room-temperature butter. Rest wrapped in a cooler for at least 2 hours. Slice the flat pencil-thick against the grain, then turn the point 90 degrees and slice that separately.
recipes.cooksNote: Temperature is a guide, feel is the answer. Two briskets of the same weight can finish 3°C apart, and probe tenderness is the only reliable test.

recipes.title: Apple Pie
recipes.description: Double crust, mixed apples, and enough thickener that the filling holds when you cut it. Cold butter, cold water, minimum handling.

items: 250 g very cold unsalted butter, cubed
120 ml ice water, plus 1 tbsp cider vinegar
1.4 kg apples, half tart (Granny Smith) and half sweet (Braeburn or Honeycrisp), peeled and sliced 8 mm
150 g sugar, half of it brown
1½ tsp cinnamon, ¼ tsp nutmeg, ¼ tsp allspice
Juice and zest of ½ lemon

method: Cut the butter into the flour, sugar, and salt until you have pieces ranging from pea-sized to almond-sized. Those flat sheets of butter become the flaky layers.
Add the ice water and vinegar and toss with a fork until it just holds when squeezed. Divide, flatten into discs, wrap, and chill 2 hours.
Toss the apples with the sugar, spices, lemon, and salt. Leave 45 minutes, then drain the juice into a pan.
Reduce that juice to about 4 tbsp of syrup, then toss it back through the apples with the cornstarch. This step is why the pie won't be watery.
Roll the bottom crust, line a 23 cm pie dish, and chill. Pile in the filling, mounding it high, and dot with butter.
Roll the top crust, lay it over, trim, seal, crimp, and cut steam vents. Chill 30 minutes. A cold pie going into a hot oven holds its shape.
Bake at 220°C for 20 minutes, then 190°C for 40 to 50 minutes until the juices bubble thickly through the vents. Cool at least 4 hours before cutting.
recipes.cooksNote: Four hours of cooling feels absurd and it's the difference between a slice and a puddle. The starch needs to set completely, and a warm pie has not set.

recipes.title: Pizza Napoletana
recipes.description: Two-day dough, blistered edge, soupy centre. Home ovens can't reach 450°C, so the fix is a very hot steel or stone plus the grill element.

items: 600 g Italian 00 flour, W280 or higher
0.6 g fresh yeast, or a scant ¼ tsp instant
80 g San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand, salted, nothing else added
70 g fior di latte or buffalo mozzarella, torn and drained

method: Dissolve the salt in the water, then add about a tenth of the flour and whisk. Crumble in the yeast, then add the rest of the flour.
Mix to a rough dough, rest 20 minutes, then knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Rest covered for 2 hours at room temperature.
Divide into four 245 g balls, shaping each tightly with a closed seam underneath.
Store in a lidded container and refrigerate 24 hours, then bring back to room temperature for 3 hours before baking. They should look domed and relaxed.
Heat your oven as hot as it goes with a steel or stone on the upper rack for at least 45 minutes. Switch to the grill element 10 minutes before baking.
Stretch a ball on a floured surface using your fingertips from the centre outward, always leaving the outer 2 cm untouched. That untouched ring becomes the cornicione. Never use a rolling pin.
Top quickly: tomato first, then cheese, then a drizzle of oil. Bake 5 to 7 minutes until the crust is puffed and spotted. Add basil as it comes out.
recipes.cooksNote: Drain the mozzarella on paper towels for an hour beforehand. Wet cheese is the main cause of a soggy centre at home.

recipes.title: Prosciutto di San Daniele
recipes.description: A protected ham from Friuli, cured with nothing but sea salt for at least 13 months. You can't make it, and you shouldn't try. What you can do is serve it properly, which most people don't.

items: 200 g Prosciutto di San Daniele, sliced to order

method: Buy it sliced fresh from the counter, not vacuum packed. Ask for it cut thin enough to see light through, but not so thin it shreds.
Ask them to layer the slices between paper. Stacked slices weld together and tear when you separate them.
Take it out of the fridge 30 minutes before serving. Cold ham has almost no aroma, and the fat stays waxy instead of melting.
Lay the slices loosely on a plate in soft folds. Flat overlapping slices look tidy and eat worse.
Add the burrata, torn open, and the fruit cut into wedges or halves.
Drizzle olive oil over the cheese only, not the ham. The ham has enough fat of its own.
Crack pepper over, scatter the rocket, and serve with grissini. No vinegar, no balsamic glaze.
recipes.cooksNote: If you're wrapping melon, do it at the last second. The fruit's moisture makes the ham slippery and dulls the salt within a few minutes.

recipes.title: Tajarin al Tartufo Bianco
recipes.description: Piedmontese egg noodles, cut thin as thread, with a lot of yolks and very little else. White truffle season runs October to December and the truffle is never cooked, only shaved.
method: Mound the flour, make a well, and add the yolks, oil, and salt. Work them in with a fork, drawing flour from the inside wall.
Knead 10 minutes until smooth and quite firm. It'll feel stiffer than normal pasta dough because of the yolk ratio. Wrap and rest 1 hour.
Roll in a machine down to the second-thinnest setting, or by hand until nearly translucent.
Flour the sheet well, fold it loosely, and cut into strands 1 to 2 mm wide. Toss with semolina and leave in loose nests.
Melt the butter gently in a wide pan until foaming but not coloured.
Boil the tajarin in well-salted water for 60 to 90 seconds. Lift straight into the butter with tongs, add pasta water, and toss hard for 30 seconds so it emulsifies.
Take off the heat, add the cheese, and toss again. Plate, then shave the truffle over at the table so the smell hits everyone at once.
recipes.cooksNote: Buy truffle by weight the day you're cooking. It loses aroma fast, and a three-day-old white truffle is an expensive disappointment.

recipes.title: Pasta 'ncasciata
recipes.description: Sicilian baked pasta with aubergine, meat, egg, and caciocavallo. Rich and structured enough to slice, and Montalbano's favourite dish, if you follow the books.

items: 400 g minced beef or a mix of beef and pork

method: Salt the aubergine slices and leave 30 minutes, then rinse and dry. Fry in olive oil until golden on both sides and drain on paper.
Soften the onion and garlic in oil, add the mince, and brown it hard.
Add the wine and reduce, then the passata. Simmer 40 minutes until thick and dark. Season and tear in basil.
Boil the pasta 3 minutes short of al dente. It finishes in the oven.
Toss the drained pasta with two thirds of the sauce and half the Pecorino.

Oil a deep dish and line the base and sides with fried aubergine. Fill with half the pasta, then the egg slices, salami, and cubed cheese. Add the rest of the pasta, remaining sauce, and any leftover aubergine on top.
Cover with breadcrumbs and Pecorino and bake at 190°C for 30 minutes. Rest 15 minutes before cutting, or it collapses.
recipes.cooksNote: Frying the aubergine gives a better texture than roasting, but roasting at 220°C with oil uses a quarter of the oil and is a fair trade on a weeknight.

recipes.title: Pappardelle al Ragù di Cinghiale
recipes.description: Wide ribbons with a slow wild boar ragù. Pork shoulder works if boar isn't available, and the marinade is what tames the gaminess.

items: 1 kg wild boar shoulder, cubed, or pork shoulder
750 ml red wine, Chianti or similar
2 bay leaves, 6 juniper berries, 1 cinnamon stick
1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks, finely diced

method: Marinate the meat overnight in half the wine with the bay, juniper, and cinnamon. Drain and dry it, discarding the marinade.
Make the pasta: mound the flour, add eggs and yolks, knead 10 minutes, rest 1 hour wrapped.
Brown the meat hard in olive oil, in batches. Set aside.
Cook the soffritto slowly in the same pot for 15 minutes until soft and sweet.
Return the meat, add the remaining wine and reduce by half, then the tomatoes, paste, stock, and rosemary. Simmer, barely bubbling, for 2½ hours.
Shred the meat with two forks in the pot and reduce until thick. Season.
Roll the pasta to 1 mm and cut into 2.5 cm ribbons. Boil 2 minutes, then toss with the ragù and a splash of pasta water in the pan. Cheese at the table.
recipes.cooksNote: Ragù should coat the pasta, not sit in a pool. If yours is loose, boil it hard uncovered for 10 minutes before saucing.

recipes.title: Strudel di Mele
recipes.description: Alto Adige apple strudel. The pastry is a stretched dough, not puff, and thin enough to read newsprint through. The breadcrumbs are structural, not filler.

items: 1 kg tart apples, peeled and sliced thin
80 g raisins soaked in 3 tbsp rum
80 g breadcrumbs fried in 60 g butter until golden

method: Knead the dough ingredients for 10 minutes until very smooth and elastic. Brush with oil, cover with a warm bowl, and rest 1 hour.
Toss the apples with sugar, cinnamon, lemon, raisins, and nuts. Let the mixture sit 10 minutes, then drain off the juice that collects.
Spread a clean tablecloth on the table and flour it. Roll the dough out, then work your floured hands underneath and stretch it outward from the centre, walking around the table.
Keep going until it's about 50 by 70 cm and translucent. Trim the thick edges off.
Brush with melted butter, scatter the fried breadcrumbs over two thirds, and pile the apples along the near edge.
Lift the cloth and let it roll the strudel over on itself. Tuck the ends under and slide it onto a lined tray, seam down, curving it if needed.
Brush with butter and bake at 190°C for 40 to 45 minutes, brushing twice more. Cool 20 minutes, dust with icing sugar, and serve with cream.
recipes.cooksNote: Tears happen. Patch them with a scrap of dough and keep going, since the roll hides everything.

recipes.title: Canederli con Formaggio
recipes.description: Bread dumplings from the Dolomites, made with stale bread and cheese, served either in broth or with browned butter. Peasant food that outlived its poverty.

items: 300 g stale white bread, cut into 1 cm cubes
150 g cheese: a mix of smoked scamorza, Fontina, and a hard aged cheese
1 small onion, finely chopped and softened in butter
3 tbsp plain flour, plus more if needed
1.5 litres beef broth, or 80 g butter and sage

method: Pour the warm milk over the bread cubes and leave 20 minutes, turning once. The bread should be soft throughout and not swimming.
Beat the eggs with salt, pepper, and nutmeg, then mix into the bread along with the cheese, onion, and herbs.
Squeeze the mixture through your fingers until it holds together. Add the flour a spoonful at a time until you can shape a ball that doesn't slump.
Rest 15 minutes. Roll into balls the size of a small apple, about 70 g each, with damp hands.
Test one in barely simmering salted water for 12 minutes. If it disintegrates, add another spoon of flour to the mix.
Poach the rest for 15 minutes at a gentle simmer. Boiling breaks them apart.
Serve in hot broth, or drained and dressed with butter browned with sage leaves and a shower of grated cheese.
recipes.cooksNote: Fresh bread will not work. It turns to paste. If your bread isn't stale, dry the cubes in a low oven for 20 minutes first.

recipes.title: Risotto alla Trevigiana
recipes.description: Risotto with radicchio di Treviso, which turns the rice a strange purple-grey and tastes pleasantly bitter against the wine and cheese.

items: 1 small onion or 2 shallots, very finely chopped
1.2 litres chicken or vegetable stock, kept hot
150 ml dry red wine, or Prosecco
60 g butter, half cold and cubed

method: Sweat the onion in the oil and half the butter over low heat for 8 minutes without colouring.
Add two thirds of the radicchio and cook 5 minutes until wilted and soft.
Add the rice and toast it for 2 minutes, stirring, until the grains look chalky at the edges and translucent at the centre.
Pour in the wine and stir until it's fully absorbed.
Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring often, waiting until each addition is nearly absorbed before the next. About 17 minutes total.
Add the remaining raw radicchio in the last 3 minutes so some of it stays sharp.
Take off the heat, beat in the cold butter and cheese hard for a full minute, then rest covered 2 minutes. It should ripple when you shake the pan.
recipes.cooksNote: That final vigorous beating is called mantecatura and it's what makes risotto creamy. Do it off the heat, with cold butter, and don't be gentle.

recipes.title: Tiramisu
recipes.description: Coffee, mascarpone, eggs, savoiardi. The classic version uses raw eggs, which many people would rather avoid, so this one cooks the yolks into a zabaglione instead.
method: Whisk the yolks, sugar, and Marsala in a bowl over simmering water for 8 to 10 minutes until thick, pale, and hot to the touch, around 70°C. Whisk constantly so it doesn't scramble.
Cool the zabaglione over ice, whisking now and then, until it's at room temperature.
Beat the mascarpone briefly until smooth. Overworking makes it grainy.
Fold the zabaglione into the mascarpone.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it in gently.
Mix the espresso with the liqueur. Dip each savoiardo for one second per side. One second. They keep absorbing after they leave the coffee.
Layer biscuits and cream twice in a dish, smooth the top, and chill at least 6 hours. Dust with cocoa immediately before serving, never before.
recipes.cooksNote: Use hard savoiardi, not soft sponge fingers. Soft ones turn to sludge instantly and you'll get a coffee-flavoured puddle.

recipes.title: Guanciale
recipes.description: Cured pork jowl, and the correct fat for carbonara, amatriciana, and gricia. It takes three weeks and almost no effort, and it costs a fraction of buying it.

items: 1.2 kg pork jowl, skin on, glands trimmed out
35 g fine sea salt (about 3% of the meat weight)
3 g curing salt #2, optional but sensible for a long cure
20 g coarse black pepper, plus more for coating

method: Trim the jowl into a neat rectangle and remove any glands, which look like pale firm lumps. They taste bad.
Weigh the trimmed meat and recalculate the salt at 3% if it's changed much.
Mix all the cure ingredients and rub them into every surface, pressing hard.
Put it in a bag or non-reactive container, cover, and refrigerate 7 days, turning daily and redistributing the liquid that draws out.
Rinse thoroughly, pat dry, and coat the meat side heavily in fresh cracked pepper.
Pierce a corner, tie with string, and hang somewhere cool and humid: 12 to 15°C at 65 to 75% humidity. A cellar, a wine fridge, or a spare fridge with a bowl of water in it.
It's ready when it has lost about 30% of its post-cure weight, usually 2 to 3 weeks. Firm all the way through with no soft spots. Wrap and keep refrigerated for months.
recipes.cooksNote: White powdery mould is normal and harmless. Wipe it with vinegar. Green, black, or fuzzy mould means throw it out, no debate.

recipes.title: Panzerotti
recipes.description: Fried filled dough from Puglia. Half-moon shaped, tomato and mozzarella inside, and hot enough on the first bite to be a genuine hazard.

items: 300 g mozzarella, diced and drained overnight
Optional: anchovy, capers, or diced cooked ham

method: Mix the dough and knead 8 minutes until smooth. Rise 2 to 3 hours until doubled.
Drain both the mozzarella and the tomatoes properly. Wet filling causes bursting, and bursting in hot oil is genuinely dangerous.
Season the tomatoes with oregano, salt, pepper, and a little oil.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a 14 cm circle about 3 mm thick.
Put a spoonful of tomato and a few cubes of cheese slightly off-centre. Don't overfill, leave a clear 2 cm border.
Fold over, press the air out from the filling outward, and seal by pressing with a fork or by folding and crimping the edge.
Fry in oil at 175°C for 2 to 3 minutes a side until deep golden and puffed. Drain on a rack and wait five minutes before eating.
recipes.cooksNote: Any panzerotto with a weak seal will open in the pan. Check each one before it goes in, and fry the suspect ones last.

recipes.title: Erbazzone Reggiano
recipes.description: A flat savoury pie from Reggio Emilia, filled with chard, Parmigiano, and lardo or pancetta. Thin crust, thick filling, and it's just as good cold.

items: 80 g lard or 90 g olive oil
1.2 kg Swiss chard or spinach, stalks removed
A little lard or oil for the top

method: Work the flour, lard, salt, and water into a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes, wrap, and rest 30 minutes.
Boil the chard 3 minutes, drain, cool, then squeeze it dry with real force. Chop it fine.
Render the pancetta, then add the onions, spring onions, and garlic and cook 8 minutes until soft.
Mix the chard with the onion mixture, cheese, eggs, breadcrumbs, and plenty of nutmeg and pepper. Season carefully since the pancetta and cheese are both salty.
Roll two thirds of the dough very thin and line a 28 cm tin, letting it overhang.
Spread the filling flat, roll the remaining dough into a thin lid, seal the edges, and trim.
Prick all over with a fork, rub the top with lard, and bake at 200°C for 40 to 45 minutes until browned and crisp. Cool 20 minutes before cutting.
recipes.cooksNote: Squeeze the greens harder than you think necessary. A cup of water left in the chard will make the bottom crust soggy every time.

recipes.title: Crespelle alla Valdostana
recipes.description: Crêpes rolled around ham and Fontina, baked in béchamel. From Valle d'Aosta, and Fontina is the one ingredient that doesn't substitute well.

items: 60 g butter, 60 g flour, 700 ml milk

method: Whisk the crêpe ingredients into a smooth thin batter and rest 30 minutes.
Cook 12 thin crêpes in a lightly buttered 20 cm pan, about a minute a side. Stack them and set aside.
For the béchamel, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 2 minutes. Add the milk gradually, whisking, and simmer until it coats a spoon. Season with nutmeg.
Lay a slice of ham and a few slices of Fontina on each crêpe, add a spoonful of béchamel, and roll into a cylinder.
Spread a layer of béchamel in a buttered baking dish.
Arrange the rolls seam side down, pour the rest of the béchamel over, and scatter the Parmigiano and dots of butter.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, then grill for 3 minutes until the top blisters. Rest 5 minutes.
recipes.cooksNote: Fontina releases a lot of oil when it melts. That's normal and it's the best part, so don't try to blot it.

recipes.title: Arrosticini
recipes.description: Abruzzese sheep skewers. Small cubes of mutton on thin wooden sticks, grilled fast over a long narrow brazier. Salt is the only seasoning and that's not an omission.

items: 1 kg mutton or hogget leg and shoulder, ideally with some fat
100 g sheep fat, if your meat is lean
Bread and red wine to serve

method: Chill the meat until very firm, almost frozen at the edges. It cuts far more cleanly.
Cut into cubes of about 1.5 cm. Small and even. This is the whole technique.
Thread 8 to 10 cubes onto each skewer, alternating a piece of fat every third cube. Push them together tightly so they protect each other from the heat.
Trim the ends flat with scissors so the skewers sit evenly.
Build a charcoal fire and rake it into a narrow bed. Traditionally the skewers rest across a channel so only the meat sits over the coals and the sticks stay cool.
Grill 2 to 3 minutes a side over high heat, turning once. Salt them as they come off.
Serve immediately on a pile, with bread rubbed with olive oil and warmed on the grill. Eat with your hands, straight from the skewer.
recipes.cooksNote: Resist marinating them. Arrosticini are about sheep and fire, and anything else you add is just covering up the meat.

recipes.title: Mezzelune
recipes.description: Half-moon filled pasta, most often ricotta and spinach in the north, dressed with butter and sage. Bigger than ravioli, quicker to make, harder to overfill.

items: 250 g spinach, cooked and squeezed bone dry

method: Make the dough, knead 10 minutes, and rest wrapped for 45 minutes.
Chop the squeezed spinach finely and mix with ricotta, Parmigiano, yolk, zest, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Taste it. It should be seasoned assertively, because pasta dilutes everything.
Roll the dough to about 1 mm, working with one piece at a time and keeping the rest covered.
Cut 8 cm circles with a cutter or glass.
Pipe or spoon a heaped teaspoon into the centre of each. Brush the edge with water only if the dough has dried out.
Fold over and seal, pressing outward from the filling to push all the air out. Trapped air makes them burst.
